Who was the leading Belgravian in the 1994 London Marathon as the field headed over Tower Bridge? Well, Gary Staines was doing the pace making at that point although also near the leaders were Paul Evans and Kassa Tadesse - must be Gary.

Gary Staines was there to act as pace-maker for Eamon Martin and at Tower Bridge was leading a very large pack which included a slightly unhappy looking Paul Evans and about a minute further back was Kassa Tadesse.

Gary Staines and one time World CC Champ Treacy were forcing the pace at 3k in 8:31, heading a bunch of seven that included Kassa and Rossendale's Dave Lewis. 5k was reached in 14:40 and at 6k, 17:32, Staines and Strizhakov of Russia were dropped when Treacy applied even more pressure.

Gary Staines has also been running into good winter form following his super series of Autumn runs on the road and both turned out to compete in the Durham International Cross Country Race on the last day of 1994.
Belgrave were very well represented: Kassa Tadesse ranked 8th with five races and 607 points, Darren Mead 24th from four races with 393, and Gary Staines 49th from two races with 246.

Whereas Kassa was in command, however, the Aldershot man had already overcooked things and by the end of the first circuit it was a cool and calm looking Gary Staines who had joined Kassa along with Harris of Boxhill.

Not at all happy either with his day's work was Paul Edwards who only allowed two of his efforts to be measured and Gary Staines' confidence also took a knock in the 10k as he barely cracked the half-hour.

The opening day of competition saw a much better race from Gary Staines than he had put together recently. Just bear in mind that four years ago this man was silver medallist in Split, Yugolslavia, over 5,000m but has since then been travelling a hard road littered with set-backs.

Back on the track Gary Staines was one of only three winners for the Bels., a strong last lap in the 1500 getting him home ahead of a pack of good class club runners who were snapping at his heels down the straight.

As Helsinki bound Gary Staines lined up for the 800 he was described by the announcer as "a flash sort of guy". But there's a lot of difference between the 25 laps of Gary's specialist distance and the two circuits demanded here - especially when the league throws up athletes that delight in 'having a pop' at a 'name'.
